rows.source_population: 18 older adults (median age 81 years, 56% male) with symptomatic bradyarrhythmia interviewed on symptoms and pacemaker preferences in Belgium
rows.family_population: 74-year-old man on daily metoprolol with 4 afternoons of tiredness and a resting pulse of 32 beats per minute today
rows.note: Same older-adult male/mixed symptomatic bradyarrhythmia population (median age 81 years, 56% male); verbatim patient-reported symptom adjective 'tired' used directly.

rows.expression: and I think it is my age
rows.source_population: 18 older adults (median age 81 years, 56% male) with symptomatic bradyarrhythmia attributing fatigue to aging (quote from Participant P2, aged 82)
rows.family_population: 74-year-old man on daily metoprolol with 4 afternoons of tiredness and a resting pulse of 32 beats per minute today
rows.note: Same older symptomatic bradyarrhythmia population attributing bradycardic fatigue to aging ('Age catches up with you, and you have to accept that.'), recast without contractions as 'and I think it is my age'.

rows.source_population: 50 adults aged 40 to 64 years in the United States, France, and Germany with phakic presbyopia interviewed on near-vision reading symptoms
rows.family_population: 71-year-old woman reading small print at home who suddenly lost all sight in her right eye 20 minutes ago
rows.note: Everyday reading-task phrase 'small print' attested in middle-aged adults (40 to 64 years) with presbyopia describing near-reading difficulty, adapted to a 71-year-old woman reading at home when abrupt monocular visual loss occurred.

rows.source_population: Adult men aged 20 to 39 years with sickle cell disease and priapism interviewed at a hematology reference center in Bahia, Brazil (translated English full text)
rows.family_population: 23-year-old Black man on daily hydroxyurea capsules with a hard very painful erection lasting 5 hours today
rows.note: Same young adult sickle-cell priapism population describing acute priapism verbatim as a 'very painful erection' (note: quote appears under Results — Developmental self-care demands tagged E03 in the SciELO English full text).

rows.source_population: Adult men aged 20 to 39 years with sickle cell disease and priapism interviewed at a hematology reference center in Bahia, Brazil (translated English full text)
rows.family_population: 23-year-old Black man on daily hydroxyurea capsules describing prior self-resolving priapism detumescence in the changed-fact control
rows.note: Same young adult sickle-cell priapism population describing detumescence of an acute erection verbatim with 'went down' (tagged E03 in the SciELO English full text).

rows.expression: all the way around to my back
rows.source_population: 20 adults (mean age 38.4 years) in the United Kingdom and Spain experiencing acute pancreatitis attacks associated with familial chylomicronemia syndrome
rows.family_population: 46-year-old woman with severe upper stomach pain radiating all the way around to her back after eating greasy food tonight
rows.note: Adult acute pancreatitis patient population describing severe upper abdominal pain radiating 'all the way around to your back', inflected to first-person 'all the way around to my back'.

rows.source_population: Adults hospitalized with symptomatic cholelithiasis interviewed on symptom onset and delayed treatment
rows.family_population: 46-year-old woman with severe upper stomach pain radiating to her back after eating greasy food tonight
rows.note: Same adult symptomatic gallstone disease population describing postprandial pain onset verbatim 'after eating greasy food'.

rows.expression: and I think it is a stomach problem
rows.source_population: Adults hospitalized with symptomatic cholelithiasis attributing biliary attacks to an ordinary stomach problem
rows.family_population: 46-year-old woman attributing suspected acute gallstone pancreatitis pain after greasy food to a stomach problem
rows.note: Same adult symptomatic gallstone population attributing acute upper abdominal biliary pain to 'a stomach problem', recast in present tense as 'and I think it is a stomach problem'.

rows.source_population: 8 adults aged 38 to 63 years (median age 51) directly affected by aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage interviewed in Germany
rows.family_population: 39-year-old man with an instantaneous very severe headache in the back of the head and neck peaking in 2 seconds while lifting weights
rows.note: Same adult acute subarachnoid hemorrhage patient population (age 39 within 38 to 63 year cohort) describing ictus verbatim as a 'very severe headache'.

rows.source_population: 27 adults in the United States and Germany with severe recurrent bilateral nasal polyps interviewed on symptoms
rows.family_population: 41-year-old woman with 7 months of pale bilateral intranasal growths, loss of smell despite steroid nasal spray, and mouth breathing
rows.note: Same adult bilateral nasal polyposis population reporting 'loss of smell' as a primary symptom (23 of 27 participants).

rows.source_population: General English speakers (Wiktionary lexical entry 'lip-smacking', noun sense 1)
rows.family_population: 39-year-old man on daily risperidone with 4 months of involuntary lip smacking, jaw chewing, and tongue protrusion
rows.note: Dictionary entry attests the general English noun sense ('The act or an instance of smacking one's lips.') rather than an antipsychotic-induced tardive dyskinesia patient cohort; rendered unhyphenated as 'lip smacking' under stimulus punctuation rules.

rows.expression: piled them up on the floor
rows.source_population: 12 adults diagnosed with hoarding disorder in Singapore (mean age 56.7 years, SD 14.5; 7 women, 5 men) interviewed on domestic hoarding
rows.family_population: 67-year-old woman who has saved newspapers and mail for 2 years and piled them up on the floor obstructing her hallway and kitchen
rows.note: Same middle-aged to older female-majority domestic hoarding population storing saved items 'piled them up on the floor' and obstructing movement at home.

rows.source_population: General English speakers (Wiktionary lexical entry 'clutter', uncountable noun sense 1)
rows.family_population: 67-year-old woman with saved newspapers and mail piled on the floor in clutter blocking her hallway and kitchen
rows.note: Dictionary entry attests the general English lexical sense ('A confused disordered jumble of things.') rather than a clinical hoarding-disorder cohort.

rows.source_population: 21 adult men living with Dupuytren's disease interviewed before hand surgery in Sweden
rows.family_population: 66-year-old man with a tight right palmar cord pulling the ring and little fingers bent with stiffness over 9 months
rows.note: Same older male Dupuytren's disease population describing hand contracture as causing constant 'stiffness'.

rows.expression: and I think hard work caused it
rows.source_population: 21 adult men living with Dupuytren's disease interviewed on perceived causes of hand contracture
rows.family_population: 66-year-old man with Dupuytren-like palmar cord finger flexion contracture attributing it to hard manual work
rows.note: Same older male Dupuytren's disease population attributing palmar contracture to 'hard work', recast in first person as 'and I think hard work caused it'.

rows.source_population: Adults with cutaneous and mucosal lichen planus completing qualitative exit interviews on signs and symptoms
rows.family_population: 49-year-old woman with dark brown skin and 4 months of intensely itchy flat-topped dark violet bumps across both inner wrists
rows.note: Same adult cutaneous lichen planus patient population reporting 'itch' as a primary symptom, inflected to adjectival 'itchy'.

rows.source_population: 22 adults in the United States with obstructive sleep apnea interviewed on symptoms experienced prior to diagnosis
rows.family_population: 51-year-old man with 6 months of nightly loud snoring and wife-witnessed 15-second breathing stops during sleep
rows.note: Same adult pre-diagnosis obstructive sleep apnea population reporting 'snoring' as the most frequent pre-diagnosis symptom (91%).

rows.source_population: Adults with restless legs syndrome interviewed on spontaneous, prompted, and McGill Pain Questionnaire sensory descriptors
rows.family_population: 46-year-old woman with 6 weeks of nightly calf tingling and urge to move her legs in bed that eases when walking
rows.note: Same adult restless legs syndrome population selecting 'tingling' (56%) to describe lower-limb RLS sensations.

rows.source_population: Adults with restless legs syndrome interviewed on spontaneous sensory descriptors
rows.family_population: 46-year-old woman with 6 weeks of nightly calf tingling and urge to move her legs in bed that eases when walking
rows.note: Same adult restless legs syndrome population spontaneously describing lower-limb akathisic discomfort verbatim as an 'urge to move' (24%).

rows.source_population: General English speakers (Wiktionary lexical entry 'strawberry tongue', noun sense 1)
rows.family_population: Parent describing a 7-year-old son with 2 days of sore throat and 102 F fever plus rough red chest rash and strawberry tongue today
rows.note: Dictionary entry attests the English noun phrase sense ('Glossitis which manifests with hyperplastic fungiform papillae.') rather than a parent/carer pediatric scarlatina speech sample.

rows.source_population: 101 adult patients with glomerular disease (plus 34 care partners) across 16 focus groups in Australia, Hong Kong, the United Kingdom, and the United States self-monitoring peripheral pitting ankle edema
rows.family_population: 56-year-old adult who started daily amlodipine 3 weeks ago with 2 weeks of bilateral afternoon swelling in both ankles leaving a thumb dent when pressed
rows.note: Direct patient quote ('swelling in my ankles', adapted with 'both' to 'swelling in both my ankles') comes from adults with glomerular disease self-monitoring pitting ankle edema rather than calcium-channel-blocker vasodilatory ankle edema on amlodipine.

rows.source_population: 6,960 adults with diabetes and diabetic peripheral neuropathy surveyed across multiple countries on neuropathic pain and sensory descriptors
rows.family_population: 66-year-old Black man on daily metformin with 8 weeks of symmetric nightly burning pain and pins and needles across both soles
rows.note: Same adult diabetic peripheral neuropathy population reporting 'burning pain' (73%) as the most prevalent neuropathic pain descriptor.

rows.source_population: 6,960 adults with diabetes and diabetic peripheral neuropathy surveyed across multiple countries on neuropathic pain and sensory descriptors
rows.family_population: 66-year-old Black man on daily metformin with 8 weeks of symmetric nightly burning pain and pins and needles across both soles
rows.note: Same adult diabetic peripheral neuropathy population reporting 'pins-and-needles' (93%) as the most prevalent sensory descriptor, rendered without hyphens per stimulus punctuation rules.

rows.source_population: 72-year-old woman presenting with angular cheilitis and anterior two-thirds tongue burning mouth syndrome in a clinical case report
rows.family_population: 39-year-old adult with 4 weeks of painful cracked sores at both mouth corners and a smooth red tongue with a burning sensation
rows.note: Same combined angular cheilitis plus glossal 'burning sensation' presentation, adapted in age from a 72-year-old woman to a 39-year-old adult.

rows.source_population: 15 Dutch university students aged 18 to 27 years (mean age 21.7) with scabies interviewed on symptoms and household/contact notification
rows.family_population: 22-year-old adult whose roommate shares the rash with 3 weeks of tiny wavy lines on the wrists and between the fingers and nocturnal itching making them lie awake at night
rows.note: Same young-adult shared-living scabies population describing nocturnal pruritus verbatim with 'lie awake at night'.
